title: Web front-end (interactive car builder & race UI)
description: The interactive front-end that lets a kid (12-17) actually drive the simulator: configure a car (weight, placement, wheels, axle, body, alignment), race it, watch the run animate on the track, read a plain-language 'where did your speed go?' breakdown + 'why', and save/load designs in a local garage. Folds in the former 0002 presentation layer (0003 owns both the pure RaceResult->kid-language translation AND the UI). Platform: static web app running the pure Python engine in-browser via Pyodide (WASM), hosted free on GitHub Pages; no network at runtime, all assets same-origin, no PII. Build deferred until the 0001 engine contract (CarDesign/RaceResult) stabilizes. PRD/TRD authored and APPROVED 2026-06-02; all 3 open questions resolved (audience 12-17 skewed young; stack = vanilla TS+Vite+canvas+vendored Pyodide; two non-finish modes distinguished per AC-R4).

open_questions.question: Reconcile the profile's target audience (currently ~7-12) to 12-17, matching this feature and the 0001 PRD/spec? (Side effect: a follow-up profile update that also governs 0005 educational content.)
open_questions.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-06-02 by user: reconcile to 12-17, but tune reading level and tone to the YOUNGER end (~12) so the youngest target users aren't left behind (still legible for 17). PRD A2/§1/§2 and §9 updated. A follow-up profile update to 12-17 (also governing 0005) is required and is flagged for the synthesizer.

open_questions.question: Confirm the front-end stack: vanilla TypeScript + Vite + HTML canvas, with Pyodide vendored same-origin (no CDN) - or specify a preferred framework. TRD-level choice; no effect on user-visible behavior.
open_questions.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-06-02 by user: no preference, asked for the simplest robust option with good UX. Planner selected the A5 default - vanilla TypeScript + Vite + HTML canvas with Pyodide vendored same-origin (no CDN): no framework runtime, smallest bundle, easiest to keep same-origin/offline. No effect on user-visible behavior.

open_questions.question: Presentation must distinguish the engine's TWO non-finish modes so a kid doesn't read a slow car as a crash: outcome=DNF currently covers BOTH (a) unstable wobble/crash (d_COM below the stability cliff) AND (b) a stable-but-underpowered car that simply ran out of speed short of the line (e.g. worst-case-friction builds that stall ~0.3 m short). The RaceResult already carries the trajectory showing WHERE it stopped and the normal forces showing WHY, so the translation layer can tell the two stories apart ('your car tipped/wobbled' vs 'your car ran out of speed and stopped just short'). Carried over from 0001-physics-engine WI12-ADV-006 (adjudicated 2026-06-03 as a presentation concern, not an engine defect).
open_questions.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-06-02: folded into the PRD/TRD as a requirement, then CORRECTED against the frozen 0001 source. PRD AC-R4 (new) mandates telling the two non-finish stories apart; AC-R2 reworded from 'DNF/crash' to a neutral non-finish state. Verified against engine.py/result.py: the engine emits DNF for BOTH an instability short-circuit (car never leaves the line: single trajectory point at position 0, all-zero ledger) AND an in-loop stall (multi-point trajectory ending at 0<position<track_length). The discriminator is the TRAJECTORY + LEDGER, NOT normal_forces (which is a single static front/rear pair, not a per-frame series, and cannot detect a tip). TRD present.py gains outcome in {finished, tipped, stalled} + stopped_distance_frac, a classifier on those signals (no new physics, AC-G1), distinct animator rendering (tipped = wobble-at-line with no run to animate; stalled = coast to halt), and a pytest driven by real simulate() output. A slow-but-stable car is never shown as a crash.
